name: Week 24 KB Thursday — FLOW + COMPLEX DAY 🌀 (Outside Snatch Flow 2nd Run + Brutal Complex)
description:
The fun day continues. You asked for more of the Outside Snatch Flow — here it is on its second run, this time to refine rather than just learn. It pairs with a fresh conditioning block: @Asgooch's **Brutal Complex**, here to add what the flow doesn't — a horizontal ROW and a PUSHUP.

**Warmup reminder:** halo → bottoms-up press (18lb) → figure-8 (a few slow passes) → internal core fist rotation → protective behind-back shrug, then the 7-move banded prep.

Strength runs between the two big blocks so the day isn't front-loaded. Bent press keeps its once-a-week place in the skill block. Strict press holds 50.

This day is leg-inclusive and runs long — both on purpose, both the deal you took.

dayOverview.theme: Thursday stays the flow + conditioning day. Outside Snatch Flow returns on its second run — refine the outside-arc snatch now that the order's known — paired with a different block, @Asgooch's Brutal Complex (row + pushup), chosen to fill the pull/push gap the flow leaves. Strength runs BETWEEN the two big blocks so it's not top-heavy. Bent press stays once in the skill block. Leg-inclusive and long, by design.

spotlights.why: You called the flow fun and want more of it, so the second run is about the one beat that's genuinely new to your body — the outside-arc snatch. The first time through it was enough to just get the bell overhead; now that the sequence is known, the attention goes to the arc itself: the bell traveling outside the midline and the shoulder accepting it off-plane. Punch the hand through so it rolls onto the forearm, pack the shoulder down at the catch, and make the arc smooth instead of muscled. This is the move that turns the flow from 'learned' into 'owned.'

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Thursday content rotates: W22 Outside Snatch Flow + GymFiesta circuit · W24 Outside Snatch Flow (2nd run) + Brutal Complex (@Asgooch) · W25 keep the flow, rotate the conditioning block again (the cardio complex or the upper circuit). The Outside Snatch Flow is a confirmed keeper; cycle the second block around it every week.
watchpoints: **🌀🔆 Outside Snatch Flow — 2nd run, REFINE now.** figure-8 → tactical clean → transverse lunge → outside snatch → windmill → snatch → thruster → deep squat press → hand-to-hand swing. One continuous chain per side, light bell. You know the order now — make the transitions seamless. (Canonical: kb-outside-snatch-flow.)

**🛑 The outside snatch is the spotlight beat** — the bell travels an OUTSIDE arc, off the midline. Punch the hand through, pack the shoulder DOWN at the catch, make the arc smooth. Sub a high pull if the right shoulder objects.

**🌀 Brutal Complex (@Asgooch), run circuit-style, 3 rounds.** swing → ab-stance goblet squat (alternate wide/narrow) → alternating bent-over row → close-grip pushup (hands on the bell handles). Each move for its reps, then move on, ~60s between rounds. It's here because it ADDS a row and a pushup — the pull and push the Outside Snatch Flow has none of.
**Strength runs BETWEEN the two big blocks** — flow, then strength, then complex — so the demanding volume isn't stacked at the top (the top-heavy lesson from W21).
**Bent press runs ONCE, in the skill block** 🛑 — the pattern is the anchor. Eyes on the bell, hips shift away, arm locked; it's a hinge, not a press.
**Strict overhead press holds 50 at 8/8/8** 🛑 — strict, no push-press, both sides even. KB row at 40.

**Leg-inclusive and long, on purpose.** The flow's transverse lunge, thruster, and deep squat press cost the legs the day before legs day (the complex is light on legs — it adds pull/push instead). You took the leg-cost trade. If it overruns, cut the complex to 2 rounds — not the flow.
**Protective behind-back shrug greasing set stays in the warm-up.**

exercises.notes: **LOAD:** 15-20lb. Big slow circles both directions — open the shoulders before a heavily overhead day.
**LOAD:** 18lb. Inverted bell over a vertical forearm, grip hard, shoulder packed. 8/side forward + T-plane (T-plane light). Cuff prep for the snatches.

sets.name: 🌀🔆 Outside Snatch Flow (2nd Run — Refine the Arc)
sets.notes:
**Single LIGHT bell (~18-26lb), 2 full rounds each side.** Second run — you know the order now, so this time make it seamless.

**Move #1 is the around-the-legs figure-8**, then the chain runs figure-8 → tactical clean → transverse lunge → outside snatch → windmill → snatch → thruster → deep squat press → hand-to-hand swing.

🛑 **The outside snatch is the spotlight** — the bell travels an OUTSIDE arc, off the midline, so the shoulder receives it slightly off-plane:
- **Drive from the hips**, punch the hand THROUGH so the bell rolls onto the forearm
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN** at the catch, ribs down
- **Make the arc smooth, not muscled** — that's the difference between run one and run two
- Sub a high pull if the right shoulder objects

**Reflection:** last week which transition made you stop and re-grip? Is it seamless now? And is the outside-snatch arc starting to feel natural, or still like a move you're thinking through?

sets.name: Strength — Row + Strict Press (Between the Big Blocks) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40. Hinged, flat back, bell to the hip.
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN and BACK** before the elbow moves — no shrugging the bell up
- **Elbow drives past the ribs**, not flared wide
- Slow return, full stretch at the bottom

**LOAD:** 50 across all sets — strict single-arm press, clean to rack, NO push-press.
- **Strict, ribs DOWN**, no rib flare
- **Bicep finishes by the ear, full lockout, pack the shoulder DOWN**
- Both sides to the same standard

sets.notes: 3 rounds, run BETWEEN the flow and the circuit so the demanding volume isn't stacked at the top.

sets.name: 🌀 Brutal Complex (@Asgooch) — Adds a Row + a Pushup
sets.notes:
**Single moderate bell (~20-30lb), 3 rounds, ~10-12 reps per move (each side where it alternates).** @Asgooch's Brutal Complex, chosen for what it ADDS.

**Four moves, run circuit-style** — each move for its reps, then move on. Minimal rest between moves, ~60s between rounds.

**Why this block:** the Outside Snatch Flow is all swing / snatch / clean / lunge — no real pull, no push. This block's **alternating bent-over row** and **close-grip pushup** fill both gaps, so Thursday covers the whole body instead of hammering the same patterns twice.

**The moves:**
- **Swing** — two-handed, explosive hip snap
- **Ab-stance goblet squat** — alternate WIDE and NARROW stance each rep
- **Alternating bent-over row** — hinge, flat back, row one side then the other; pack the shoulder DOWN, elbow past the ribs
- **Close-grip pushup** — hands ON the bell handles, elbows tucked; a triceps-biased push and a novel one

**If the session has run long, this drops to 2 rounds** — not the flow.

sets.name: Skill — Bent Press + Windmill 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 25-35lb. Bent press keeps its once-a-week place even though its old flow rotated off Thursday.
- **A HINGE and a side-bend, not a press** — the arm locks out and stays locked; the body moves underneath
- **Eyes on the bell** the whole way down
- **Hips shift AWAY** from the loaded side as the torso descends
- Stand up under control

**LOAD:** 18-30lb, light. Rotated in alongside the bent press.
- **Straight loaded arm, eyes on the bell**
- **Hinge to the opposite hip** — this is a hip hinge with rotation, not a side crunch
- **Slow and controlled** both directions; the QL has been busy, so keep it clean

sets.notes: 2 rounds, unhurried. Bent press appears exactly once today — the lateral-chain load is a deliberate choice.

exercises.notes: 60s each side. Hip flexor release — counters the transverse lunges, thrusters, and knee drives.
30s each side. QL — bent press and windmill ran today; give the lateral chain the downshift.

tips: **Outside Snatch Flow, 2nd run — refine, don't just repeat.** You know the order; make the transitions seamless and smooth the outside-snatch arc.
🛑 **The outside snatch travels an OUTSIDE arc** — punch the hand through, pack the shoulder down, sub a high pull if the shoulder objects.
**Brutal Complex (@Asgooch), 3 rounds circuit-style** — swing → ab-stance goblet squat → alternating bent-over row → close-grip pushup. Adds the row + pushup the flow lacks.
**Strength runs between the flow and the complex** so the day isn't top-heavy.
**Bent press once, in the skill block**; windmill rotated in beside it.
**Strict overhead press holds 50 at 8/8/8**; KB row at 40.
**Bottoms-up press + figure-8 passes in the warmup.**
**Leg-inclusive and long on purpose** — if it overruns, cut the complex to 2 rounds, not the flow.
Cooldown mandatory — pigeon, butterfly, cross-leg lateral.
Rotation ahead: W25 rotates the circuit around the Outside Snatch Flow again.
formPhilosophy: A flow you loved on the first run earns a second, but a second run isn't a repeat — it's the difference between finding the notes and playing the music. The first time through the Outside Snatch Flow the job was survival: get the order, get the bell overhead. Now the order is free, so the attention moves to the one beat that's actually new to your body, the outside arc, and to the seams between moves where you had to stop and re-grip. That's how a flow becomes yours. Everything else on the day is deliberate — strength tucked between the big blocks so nothing stacks, bent press held to once so the lateral chain is a choice, and the legs spent knowingly the day before legs day. Building decades, not weeks.
